chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal, from Sallam ibn al-Mustanir, who said:
ai.seo_question: Why do believers feel spiritual highs in the presence of the Imam but return to worldly concerns afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the natural fluctuation of the heart (qalb) between spiritual rapture and worldly attachment, distinguishing it from hypocrisy (nifaq) by framing it as a divine test for the repentant believer. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites the Prophet’s response to his companions, noting that if spiritual states were permanent, angels would embrace them, but the cycle of sin and forgiveness is essential to human nature. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on 'tawwab' (frequent repentance) as a sign of faith rather than a defect, linking the psychological experience of the believer to the broader theological concept of divine mercy.
